transcript:
Header: 2026-06-25 14:00 UTC; Duration: ~52m; Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Evelyn Park (Nebula Eng Mgr), Tom Reyes (CTO), Lina Gomez (SRE)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we're aiming to scope the POC for capacity and autoscale - reserved GPUs, burst strategy and fallback policies. quick intros?
[00:12] Evelyn: Evelyn here, I run the ML infra team, focused on inference reliability.
[00:17] Tom: Tom, CTO. we'll own sign-off and budgets.
[00:21] Lina: Lina, SRE, i'm the network and ops lead.
[00:25] Ravi: Ravi from Redwood, i'll lead the benchmark and config recommendations.

[00:40] Maya: Cool, top-level goals - success criteria for the POC: (1) throughput to meet our peak user load with p95 latency < 300ms on short replies, (2) cost target under $0.003 per 1k tokens as an internal target, (3) no data leakage and audit logs enabled. are those reasonable?
[01:05] Tom: p95 300ms is ambitious but doable for our short generation paths. the cost target is more of a guideline, we'll accept tradeoffs if latency is better.
[01:18] Evelyn: Also want regression detection in quality across prompts - we can provide a small eval set.

[01:35] Ravi: Good, thanks. a few questions on workload shape - can you share request size distribution and concurrency?
[01:44] Lina: Our traffic: 70% short prompts (<= 50 tokens), 25% medium (50-200), 5% long (>200). Peak concurrency around 900 qps across multiple routes; sustained 200-300 qps.
[02:05] Maya: Great. for a POC we usually size reserved capacity to handle baseline sustained load and then configure burst to handle spikes with autoscale or fallback to a cheaper variant.
[02:18] Tom: we're interested in reserved nodes for predictability but want burstable headroom. what does that look like in Redwood terms?

[02:30] Ravi: Two main knobs: reserved GPU pools (dedicated instances you commit for the POC window) and burst capacity that uses shared pools or overprovisioning for short periods. typical pattern: reserve enough GPUs for sustained 40-60% of peak, then allow burst to 100% for ~5-10 minutes using queued requests + fast lanes.
[02:52] Evelyn: curious about autoscale reaction times - we care about scaling up fast for sudden spikes.
[02:58] Ravi: scaling is layered - quick horizontal autoscale within the dedicated pool can add additional model workers in ~30-90s depending on model cold-starts; for model cold-start sensitive cases we recommend keeping warm replicas or using a smaller latency-optimized variant as fallback.
[03:18] Maya: also prefix/KV cache reduces repeated work on conversational flows, which reduces required GPUs. we should capture your session reuse rates.
[03:29] Lina: session reuse is high for chat flows, ~65% of requests hit same conversation prefixes. we'll share traces.

[03:45] Tom: what about fallback policies? if burst capacity isn't available, we need graceful degradation - e.g., fallback to smaller model or to cached responses.
[03:54] Ravi: Exactly. Redwood supports policy routing: route to cheaper quantized model, degrade max tokens, or gate heavy routes. we can set per-route fallback chains.
[04:10] Evelyn: ok, Security: we need SOC2, SSO with SAML, KMS integration for keys, and audit logs. any limitations for Private vs Dedicated?
[04:22] Maya: Private gives customer-managed VPC and full key control; Dedicated also supports KMS and audit logs but uses Redwood-managed infra. we'll send a security matrix.

[04:40] Ravi: On benchmarks - we recommend running a 48-hour run with synthetic traffic matching your distribution plus a focused 2-hour spike test to validate scaling. metrics: token/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, queue depth, GPU utilization, and cost/tokens.
[04:58] Lina: For GPU sizing do you recommend A100 or H100? our infra prefers H100 but it's pricier.
[05:06] Ravi: H100 generally gives better throughput per GPU, especially for large-context models, but quantization and kernel choices also matter. for short-chat workloads A100 can be cost-effective. we'll run both in the benchmark if you want.

[05:25] Tom: what's the expected GPU count for our profile? 900 qps peak, mostly short tokens, high session reuse.
[05:33] Ravi: rough napkin: if each A100 can serve 120-150 concurrent short-inference streams with caching benefits roughly, to cover sustained 300 qps you'd want ~3-4 GPUs reserved; to cover bursts to 900 you'd need up to 8-10 GPUs total if using reserved alone. recommended POC: reserve 4 GPUs and allow burst to additional 6 via shared pools. we'll validate with bench.
[06:00] Evelyn: can you be more concrete on quantization tradeoffs?
[06:04] Ravi: Sure - int8 quant gives 2-3x throughput improvements often with minimal quality hit on many models; for strict quality targets we run evals. we can produce a quantization matrix per model.

[06:20] Maya: timeline - propose: we deliver proposal and pricing by 2026-06-30, sign POC agreement by 2026-07-07, run benchmarks first week of July, and have a POC report by 2026-07-20. does that align?
[06:36] Tom: timeline ok, but need internal procurement approvals; i'll aim for sign by 7/7.

[06:45] Lina: network/VPC details - we can't open wide egress to shared pools for burst without approval; if burst goes across shared infra we need egress filters and audit.
[06:58] Ravi: We can do burst in-region only, and we have TLS + mTLS options; we'll include network requirements in the deep-dive.

[07:10] Evelyn: any gotchas on billing when mixing reserved + burst?
[07:14] Maya: Reserved is committed monthly; burst is metered. for the POC we can do a short reserved term and show actual metered cost. we'll include an example cost table in proposal.

[07:30] Tom: can Redwood simulate our SLA violations in the bench to show fallback triggers?
[07:35] Ravi: yes, we can run chaos-style scenarios: saturate GPUs, remove some nodes, and show fallback to quantized model or queueing behavior.

[07:50] (Transcription noise) Speaker 4: ummm, sorry, can you repeat the KV cache part?
[07:56] Ravi: KV cache - it's the key-value cache for transformer past states; keeps attention cache warm to avoid recomputation. sometimes transcribed as 'KVM cache' or 'K V cash', so apologies for tts errors.

[08:12] Evelyn: For impact on latency, what do we see when fallback to smaller model?
[08:17] Ravi: Smaller model typically halves latency but can degrade output quality; we'll quantify on your eval set. fallback chain can be strict: try warm replicas first, then quantized, then smaller model.

[08:35] Maya: Ok let's capture acceptance criteria clearly: (A) Bench shows p95 < 300ms for short prompts at sustained baseline, (B) scaling handles synthetic spike to 900 qps with p95 degradation under 2x baseline, (C) cost guidance provided and within target window, (D) security checklist satisfied.

[08:58] Tom: agreed. add evaluation pass/fail thresholds for quality drift on the provided eval set.

[09:10] Ravi: noted. we'll run baseline model + quantized variant + small fallback. we'll produce a per-route config recommendation: reserved GPU count, warm replica count, burst policy (max concurrent burst seconds), and fallback chain.

[09:30] Lina: On monitoring, we need token-level cost breakdown and per-route latency dashboards. can Redwood provide per-route traces?
[09:37] Maya: Yes, Redwood Console supports per-route metrics, token costs, and traces. we'll give access for the POC.

[09:50] Evelyn: One more: data residency - some of our EU users require data to stay in eu-west; can POC respect region pinning?
[09:57] Ravi: Yes, we can pin requests to eu-west region and keep logs in-region for the POC. for Private deployment you can fully control region.

[10:10] Maya: Summarizing next steps, action items and owners — we'll draft proposal + pricing, Ravi will craft benchmark plan, Lina to send traffic percentiles and SRE constraints, Tom to confirm procurement timeline.

[10:25] Tom: i'll also loop in legal for the standard DPA.

[10:35] Maya: Any other questions?

[10:38] Evelyn: none from me, thanks.

[10:40] Maya: Great, we'll follow up via email with docs and a calendar invite for the infra deep-dive. thanks all.

Notes: Transcript contains occasional mis-transcriptions and speaker overlap typical of auto-transcripts (e.g., 'KVM cache', 'kuber nets' heard). Bench plan to include 48-hour soak + 2-hour spike + chaos tests. POC proposal will include two options: Dedicated small reserved pool (4 GPUs A100) + burst up to extra 6 GPUs vs Dedicated with H100 reserved 3 GPUs and lower burst counts; cost and quality tradeoffs to be shown.

End of call.
